subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction and memoryFlush from the foreground session lane, or keep the current foreground-lane model with shorter timeouts and diagnostic recovery?
rationale: The source-backed problem is real, but the durable fix changes session ordering, transcript consistency, and delivery guarantees for interactive turns versus context maintenance.

options.title: Isolate maintenance lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency maintenance lane or worker so foreground user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for the full maintenance timeout.

options.title: Preempt foreground maintenance
options.body: Keep the current lane model but make compaction and memoryFlush abortable and reschedulable when user messages arrive, preserving stricter ordering at the cost of scheduler complexity.

options.title: Accept timeout mitigation
options.body: Treat the current 180-second default timeout and stuck-session diagnostics as sufficient, leaving foreground turns blocked during active maintenance windows.

recommendation.title: Isolate maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency maintenance lane or worker so foreground user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for the full maintenance timeout.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history most directly ties steipete to memoryFlush ownership and current foreground maintenance code, making them the best available owner for the scheduling tradeoff.
